rulings.challenge_claim: The back seam is argued in English: the cross-seam carry catchword is named without a Hebrew form or a tier, a second byte-true device straddling the same seam (the rescue pair) is left undisclosed, the burden-noun recurrence at MT 46:2 carries no quoted form and no tier and is not byte-identical, and the single-witness SAMEKH terminating MT 46:2 is filed as an interior division although it falls on the row's own back seam.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed bytes. The row carries exactly ONE Hebrew run in any field, מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier, verified as a literal substring of the source verse), so the cross-seam carry device is indeed named in English only, with no form and no tier. The load-root family crossing the Isa.46.2|Isa.46.3 seam is byte-real in every member: נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם and עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte), הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ and הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte), אֶשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte). The plene/defective disjunction verifies exactly: the plene load-bearer spelling stands in 1 verse (MT 46:1) and the defective spelling in 1 verse (MT 46:3) at skeleton tier, verse counts, with disjoint hit sets, so the tie is root-level and not a form recurrence. The rescue root verifies too: מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte) and וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte), skeleton sweep 7 verses book-wide (MT 20:6, 34:15, 37:38, 46:2, 46:4, 49:24, 49:25). The burden-noun recurrence verifies as claimed: מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte) carries tipcha and מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte) carries etnachta, so they are NOT byte-identical and match at accent_stripped tier only, while the row's 'the same noun recurs' clause supplies neither form nor tier. The role split itself is right: both sites are the burden common noun, matching the massa census's non-initial burden-noun class, not the ten verse-initial header sites. The mark: the parashah extractor keys each segment to the verse it follows, so the SAMEKH at MT 46:2 terminates that verse and falls on this row's own back seam (span Isa.46.1-Isa.46.2), while device_notes files it as an interior division and the neighbouring row opening at Isa.46.3 labels that identical segment a front-seam division (tier-3, single-witness, never a driver). TWO CORRECTIONS to the framing. (1) The challenge states that 'the span quotes both renderings of that pair (could not deliver, will deliver)'; this row quotes only web:Isa.46.1 and web:Isa.46.2, and 'Yes, I will carry, and will deliver' (web:Isa.46.4) is quoted by the NEXT row, so that premise is imported from a neighbour. (2) The rescue pair is not a 'byte-true device' as a recurrence: the two forms are byte-true in their own verses but are not byte-identical to each other, and the tie is skeleton-tier and root-level, exactly like the load-bearer pair.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). In P13-001.boundary_rationale, replace the English-only carry-catchword clause with a spliced, tier-named cross-seam disclosure: the load-root pair הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ / הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.3) answering עֲמוּס֔וֹת / נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.46.1), stating that the two load-bearer spellings are disjoint under consonantal search (1 verse each, skeleton tier, verse counts) so the tie is root-level; and add the currently undisclosed rescue root מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2) against וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4) at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide). Give the burden-noun recurrence its tier: מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1) and מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2) match at accent_stripped, not byte. In device_notes, re-file the MT 46:2 segment under this row's own back seam instead of an interior division. Tests the cure must pass, being the tests that killed the original: every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse with the normalization dry-run clean; every recurrence sentence carries an explicit tier word; every digit citation names its swept object before the number; the ref-mirror check stays green with oshb:Isa.46.3 and oshb:Isa.46.4 present; the mark-symmetry sweep stays green with the segment's division correctly located. NEW FINDING carried with this order (cross-part scope, do NOT repair row-locally): every parashah, paseq and K/Q ref in the seven p13 rows is written with a web: prefix (34 mark refs in this cluster) although that layer is MT-keyed, while the p14 rows in the adjoining cluster write the same layer with oshb: (34 refs); corpus-wide the split is 129 web-prefixed against 168 oshb-prefixed. Chapters 46-48 are identity-numbered so nothing resolves wrongly here and the mark-symmetry sweep is green, but the prefix mislabels the witness of an MT-keyed layer and would be ambiguous in either offset zone. The cure is a single corpus-wide convention pinning at owner level, not a c21 edit.

rulings.challenge_claim: The strongest rival cut inside the span, a fresh vocative under the same summons formula at Isa.46.12, is recast as an inclusio rather than disclosed as the rival, and a weaker site (Isa.46.8) is disclosed in its place; the SAMEKH terminating MT 46:11 corroborates the declined site and is never related to it; the rescue pair straddles the front seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Byte-checked. The summons pair is real and the row's tier label is right: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte) and שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte) are not byte-identical and collate identical at accent_stripped tier, which is exactly what the row says. The vocative contrast is byte-true and IS undisclosed: בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte) against אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte). The summons collocation is not exclusive to the pair, skeleton sweep 4 verses book-wide (MT 46:3, 46:12, 51:1, 51:7), verse counts, but the row makes no exclusivity claim, so nothing fails there. The SAMEKH at MT 46:11 terminates that verse, so it stands at the Isa.46.11|Isa.46.12 division; it is genuinely interior to this span (Isa.46.3-Isa.46.13) and the row's label is not wrong, so the challenge survives only in the weaker form that the segment is never related to the reading the row declines (tier-3, single-witness, corroboration only, never a driver, and its absence elsewhere never counterevidence). The rescue root crossing the FRONT seam is undisclosed: מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte) answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte), skeleton tier, 7 verses book-wide, although the row does disclose the load-root contrast at that seam by splicing the carry answer at oshb:Isa.46.4 (byte). The label collision is confirmed by census: five segments in this cluster are filed as interior by one row and front-seam by its neighbour (MT 46:2, 46:13, 47:7, 47:15, 48:11), two conventions running in the same cluster, sometimes on the same segment. FRAMING CORRECTED: this is not a rival-substitution defect. The row argues Isa.46.12 at length in its own rationale with a correctly tier-named accent_stripped inclusio claim, which is a substantive treatment and not an evasion, and the disclosed rival is a live one in the same imperative class. The real defect is evidence-completeness at Isa.46.12, where the differing vocative that the row's own front-seam logic makes decisive is never put on the page, plus the undisclosed rescue root at the front seam. SEAM-PAIR NOTE: that front-seam omission is the same defect as the neighbouring row's back-seam omission at Isa.46.2|Isa.46.3 and must be cured as ONE edit, not two, which is why severity here sits below the neighbour's.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). (1) In P13-002.boundary_rationale, where Isa.46.12 is read as the bracket closure, add the byte disclosure that the vocative differs, אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12) against בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3), and state the ground on which a repeated summons with a DIFFERENT vocative closes a bracket rather than opening a unit; note the segment terminating MT 46:11 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration of the site the row declines, never a driver. (2) Write the rescue-root cross-seam disclosure ONCE for the Isa.46.2|Isa.46.3 seam and mirror it on both sides, this row's front seam and the previous row's back seam: מַלֵּ֣ט (oshb:Isa.46.2) against וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier, sweep 7 verses book-wide. Tests the cure must pass: the seam-pair edit lands on both rows or neither; every new Hebrew run re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean; the inclusio claim keeps its accent_stripped label; the ref-mirror check stays green; the mark-symmetry sweep stays green.

rulings.challenge_claim: The ground given for holding Isa.47.4 inside the span, syntactic continuity with a surrounding sentence, is not in the pointed text, and the digit offered in the disclosed rival, '(sweep: 15 verses)', names no swept object.
rulings.grounds: Both limbs verify on the bytes. (a) oshb:Isa.47.4 is גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (byte tier; the row's own full-verse splice is byte-exact), a self-contained verbless nominal clause with no finite verb, so there is no sentence for it to be held inside. The verse before closes אֶקָּ֔ח וְלֹ֥א אֶפְגַּ֖ע אָדָֽם (oshb:Isa.47.3, byte) and is terminated by a single-witness SAMEKH; the verse after opens the fresh feminine imperative run שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי (oshb:Isa.47.5, byte). 'Holds it inside the surrounding sentence' is therefore a syntactic claim the pointed text does not carry. The row's READING is not unseated: the aside reading is right, and its real ground is the person shift from the second-person feminine imperative address on both sides to the first-person plural confession, which is what the row's own 'brief communal aside' wording already implies; only the stated ground is wrong. (b) WEB Isa 47 has 15 verses, so the offered digit is the chapter's verse count and not a count of any swept object, a semantic-class count-discipline breach, and one the universals checker cannot catch because a digit IS present. The rest of the row stands and should be preserved in repair: the title site at MT 47:4 is real (title-construct census: 25 verses book-wide, verse counts; the trisagion is a separate object), and, checked specifically against the mater-lectionis class live in this neighbourhood, MT 47:4 carries the PLENE spelling קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, byte-exact in the row's splice, distinct from the DEFECTIVE spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.49.7; the row does not blend them. The paseq at MT 47:1 is cited count-only with no intra-verse position claim, correctly.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). (i) In P13-003.boundary_rationale, replace 'holds it inside the surrounding sentence' with the person-shift ground, quoting the flanking bytes: the second-person feminine imperatives רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1) and שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי (oshb:Isa.47.5) bracketing the first-person plural verbless confession גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.47.4). (ii) In strongest_rejected_alternative, either delete the 15-verse citation or re-cut it to a genuinely swept object with its unit named before the number; a chapter verse-count may not ride in the sanctioned sweep shorthand. Tests the cure must pass, being the test that killed the original: no form or syntax claim survives that the pointed bytes do not carry, and every sweep citation names its object first and its unit; the universals check shows a digit-bearing, object-named sweep beside each universal; all splices re-collate byte; the plene spelling at oshb:Isa.47.4 is preserved exactly and never normalised toward the defective spelling at oshb:Isa.49.7.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset at Isa.47.8 is licensed by a cross-chapter 'same hear-this summons pattern' claim that carries no tier label and matches at no tier in the Hebrew, so it holds only in the English rendering.
rulings.grounds: Byte-checked, and the challenge's digits and objects all verify. MT 47:8 opens וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי זֹ֤את (oshb:Isa.47.8, byte) and MT 48:1 opens שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte). The two are not byte-identical, not accent_stripped identical, and not identical consonantally: the feminine-singular hear-this collocation stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (MT 47:8) and the masculine-plural collocation in exactly 2 (MT 48:1, MT 48:16), skeleton tier, verse counts, disjoint hit sets. The row supplies no tier for the comparison and quotes no form from the verse it compares to, so the recurrence claim ships unlabelled and unshown; that defect is REAL and upheld. FRAMING CORRECTED and severity lowered: 'matches at no tier / holds only in the English rendering' overstates. The tie is a genuine form-class tie in the Hebrew, an imperative of the hear root immediately followed by the cataphoric object and verse-initial in both places, defeated only by the person/number letter; it is a class tie rather than a form recurrence, and the row's word 'pattern' is nearer right than the challenge allows. The seam does not rest on that comparison alone: the row's own byte-quoted onset carries the verse-initial pivot particle (13 verse-initial sites book-wide, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT 47:8 among them) plus a fresh feminine-singular imperative, both byte-true. ONE ERROR IN THE CHALLENGE'S SUPPORTING PROSE: 'the second site of the plural collocation is MT 48:16, which no span in this review set quotes at all' is inaccurate, since the row two seams later splices oshb:Isa.48.16 at byte tier (וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ), as the same packet's item on that row states; what no span quotes is that verse's hear-this half.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). Re-cut the recurrence sentence in P13-004.boundary_rationale to name the object and the tier and to show the comparand: the hear-root imperative plus cataphoric object stands as feminine-singular וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי זֹ֤את (oshb:Isa.47.8) and as masculine-plural שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1), disjoint under consonantal search (1 verse and 2 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, verse counts), so the tie is class-level and not a form recurrence. Splice the oshb:Isa.48.1 comparand into this row, which currently names it in English only, and label its tier. Tests the cure must pass, being the test that killed the original: the citation sweep's Hebrew-quote-to-cited-ref binding passes for the new oshb:Isa.48.1 splice; the recurrence sentence carries an explicit tier word; every digit names its swept object and unit; the ref-mirror check stays green, web:Isa.48.1 already being in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the row declines a rival cut at Isa.48.16 without ever putting the rival's byte evidence on the page, nor Isa.48.14's, and it files the PE at MT 48:16 as an interior division although that segment terminates the verse and so divides Isa.48.16|Isa.48.17 rather than corroborating an onset AT Isa.48.16. LF: the rejected-alternative disclosure omits a candidate seam at least as strong as the one it names, Isa.48.14, with no examination of it as a rival division point and no addressee-continuity argument for passing over it.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects on one object (rival disclosure at MT 48:14 and MT 48:16), not the same defect. OL UPHELD in full on the bytes. MT 48:16 opens קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֗את (oshb:Isa.48.16, byte); its hear-this collocation שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֗את differs from שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1, byte) only in cantillation, so accent_stripped identical and not byte-identical, and consonantal search puts that collocation in exactly 2 verses book-wide, MT 48:1 and MT 48:16 (skeleton tier, verse counts). MT 48:14 opens הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.48.14, byte); its assemble-imperative stands in 2 verses book-wide (MT 45:20, MT 48:14). The row splices neither of those onsets: from MT 48:16 it splices only the closing half וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ (byte), so its central declination is argued with no form shown. The mark point is exact: the parashah extractor keys each segment to the verse it follows, so the PE at MT 48:16 terminates that verse and corroborates a division AFTER it, which is not the onset the row is arguing about, while the row files it only as an interior division (tier-3, single-witness, PE never conflated with SAMEKH, absence never counterevidence). LF REFINED on two counts. (1) The factual premise is inaccurate: the row DOES name Isa.48.14 as a declined division point, device_notes reading the material as one movement 'rather than opening a fresh row at the summons formula of Isa.48.14 or Isa.48.16', and it quotes web:Isa.48.14 in English in the rationale. The accurate finding is that the site is named without any argument and without its Hebrew, and in device_notes rather than the rival field, not that the row stayed silent on it. (2) The ranking is not established on the bytes and the evidence runs the other way: MT 48:16's collocation is accent_stripped-identical to this cluster's own summons onset at MT 48:1 and is one of only 2 sites of it book-wide, while MT 48:14's assemble-imperative shares no collocation with any seam in this cluster, its 2 sites being MT 45:20 and MT 48:14, neither a seam here. On the byte evidence the row named the STRONGER declined candidate, so this is not a case of naming the weaker of two comparable candidates.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change), ONE edit covering both items. In P13-006, splice the declined sites' bytes into the rival disclosure and move the Isa.48.14 declination out of device_notes into the rival field, or give it its ground where it stands: קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֗את (oshb:Isa.48.16), noting that its hear-this collocation matches שִׁמְעוּ זֹ֣את (oshb:Isa.48.1) at accent_stripped tier and stands in 2 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, verse counts; and הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.48.14), skeleton sweep 2 verses book-wide, with the stated ground for passing it over. Re-file the PE at MT 48:16 as terminating that verse, i.e. single-witness tier-3 corroboration for a division after Isa.48.16 and explicitly not evidence about an onset at it, with its absence before Isa.48.16 explicitly not counterevidence. Tests the cure must pass, being the test that killed the original: every declined-seam claim shows the form it declines; the mark-symmetry sweep stays green with the segment's division correctly located and PE never conflated with SAMEKH; every new Hebrew run re-collates byte with the normalization dry-run clean; the cross-row 7-gram gate stays green.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated seam ground, a bare departure imperative 'with no hear-formula', is contradicted by the span's own opening verse, where a hear-root imperative with the same object stands in the bytes, and high confidence is assigned to a bound resting on that absence statement.
rulings.grounds: Byte-checked. oshb:Isa.48.20 does carry הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את (byte), a causative plural imperative on the hear root with the identical cataphoric object the seams at MT 47:8, MT 48:1 and MT 48:16 are argued from, and consonantal search puts that causative collocation in exactly 1 verse book-wide (MT 48:20), skeleton tier, verse counts. The row's English quote renders it as an announcement, which hides the root, and the row asserts the absence of a hear-formula flatly while holding confidence high. FRAMING CORRECTED: the statement is not byte-false. The verse's ONSET is צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte) and the hear-root form stands mid-verse, as the eighth and ninth tokens, after the preceding proclamation imperative, so read of the onset, which is what the sentence is about, 'no hear-formula' is literally true. The real defect is a ROLE-SPLIT DISCLOSURE failure of exactly the class this book's discipline names for the header-versus-burden, woe-versus-invitation and divine-versus-royal frame objects: a causative proclamation directed outward and a summons addressed to the hearer are different roles on one root, and a row resting a high-confidence bound on the absence of the summons class owes that split in Hebrew rather than an unqualified absence. The secondary observation also verifies and should ride with the cure: the device_notes recurrence at web:Isa.57.21 carries no tier and quotes no form from the second site, although the substantive claim is byte-exact, אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.48.22, byte) against אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.57.21, byte) being byte-identical including accents in every token except the divine-name token, so the pair is NOT a byte-identical refrain and no refrain digit may count both under one object. What the row gets right and must keep: גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte) names its referent in-verse, so this is a named-referent servant site correctly held apart from the unnamed servant-figure zones, and the held classic is not touched. The SAMEKH terminating MT 48:22 falls on this row's own back seam and is filed as an interior division.
rulings.remedy: Author-wave work order, disclosure only (no boundary change). (i) Re-cut the seam sentence in P13-007.boundary_rationale from an absence to a role split: the onset is the departure-imperative pair צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ (oshb:Isa.48.20), and the hear-root form standing later in the same verse, הַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את (oshb:Isa.48.20), skeleton sweep 1 verse book-wide, is a causative proclamation directed outward rather than the summons-to-addressee class carried at oshb:Isa.47.8, oshb:Isa.48.1 and oshb:Isa.48.16, so it is not a competing onset. (ii) In device_notes, give the closing-verdict recurrence its tier and its second site's bytes: אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.48.22) against אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י לָרְשָׁעִֽים (oshb:Isa.57.21), byte-identical apart from the divine-name token, cited as cross-part texture only and never as boundary evidence for either seam. (iii) Re-file the MT 48:22 segment under this row's own back seam. Tests the cure must pass, being the test that killed the original: no unqualified absence claim survives where a same-root form stands inside the row's own span without a named role split; the recurrence carries an explicit tier and both sites' bytes; the citation sweep binds the oshb:Isa.57.21 splice to its cited ref; the universals check shows each remaining universal backed by an object-named, digit-bearing sweep; and if the role split cannot be sustained on the bytes, confidence drops from high rather than the sentence being kept.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: both seam grounds are asserted without the bytes, the back bound resting on an unquoted, unattributed messenger frame at Isa.49.7, the front-seam contrast mischaracterising the material it contrasts with, and the K/Q splices running through the doubled token pairs without naming which form they engage while being labelled a single byte tier. LF: device_notes misattributes the row's referent-hold argument, naming the rejected-alternative field when the argument stands in the boundary rationale.
rulings.grounds: Three items are adjudicated; two stand, one falls, and a fourth defect neither primary reached is added. LF UPHELD, checkable on the row's own text: strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only a split at web:Isa.49.4-Isa.49.5 and says nothing about the referent, while the referent tension between the naming at web:Isa.49.3 and the commissioning at web:Isa.49.5-Isa.49.6 is stated in the closing sentence of boundary_rationale, so device_notes cites the wrong field; the underlying discipline is sound and the referent is held, not decided. OL ITEM 1 UPHELD: the back-bound sentence names the fresh messenger-formula frame at web:Isa.49.7 with no form and no frame owner. rulings.grounds: Refuted on the bytes, twice over. The row's boundary_rationale carries exactly TWO Hebrew runs, the 232-character full-verse splice and the 19-character construct excerpt; both are literal substrings of oshb:Isa.49.7's source text and both collate at byte tier. Codepoint by codepoint the excerpt קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל runs qof, sheva, dalet, holam, merkha, shin, shin-dot, space, yod, hiriq, shin, SIN-DOT, SHEVA, resh, qamats, alef, tsere, tipcha, lamed, and the source at that offset carries that identical sequence with the sin dot BEFORE the sheva. That order is in fact NOT canonical combining order, the sheva's combining class sorting ahead of the sin dot's, so a canonically-normalized copy would show the OPPOSITE order from the source: the failure mode the challenge describes would have produced a visible mismatch, and there is none. Independently, the corpus-wide NFD-degradation sweep over the frozen rows lists 23 degraded quotes in 11 rows and every one is a p05 row, with zero p13 or p14 entries. The rest of the row's title handling is correct and should not be disturbed: MT 49:7 opens כֹּ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָה֩ (byte), an inventoried divine frame; the verse carries the suffixed epithet קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ (byte) and, separately, the signature title in its DEFECTIVE spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (byte), which the row quotes as attested rather than normalising it toward the plene spelling קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל that this same cluster quotes byte-exactly at oshb:Isa.47.4, so the mater-lectionis class is handled correctly on both sides.
